transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
No matter how much I rest, I feel completely drained and can’t keep up or focus at work anymore. It's gotten to the point where I'm constantly overwhelmed and just can't seem to do my job properly.
Have you been experiencing persistent feelings of sadness, hopelessness, or a lack of interest in activities you normally enjoy?

Yes, most days I wake up with this heavy, sinking feeling like there's a dark cloud sitting on my chest, and I just feel completely hopeless. I've also lost all interest in things I used to love, like jogging and my Raspberry Pi projects, so now I just end up sitting on the couch scrolling on my phone.

How long have you been experiencing these feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities, and have they been consistent or have you had any periods where you felt somewhat better?

These feelings have been going on for about a year and a bit, getting steadily worse over time. They've been consistent for most of the nearly two years since my troubles started, except for a brief stretch late last summer when my mood lifted slightly and I felt more numb than deeply sad.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'a year and a bit' and whether you've had any previous episodes of feeling this way before the past two years?

The constant low mood and feeling like a failure started about a year and a bit ago, right after I took on extra shifts and my evening classes got a lot harder. Before these past two years, I had never felt this way in my life—everything only started when the clinic changed its record system and I began my classes.

Can you clarify if your current episode of feeling low, hopeless, and uninterested in activities has lasted continuously for the past two years, or if there have been any clear breaks or periods where your mood significantly improved for more than a couple of months?

There haven't been any long breaks or significant improvements lasting several months; the heavy depression and loss of interest have been pretty continuous for over a year now. The only exception was a very brief stretch late last summer where my mood lifted slightly, but even during those few weeks, I still heard the voice and felt like I was being tracked. Aside from that brief time, the hopeless feeling has been there almost the entire time.

Can you confirm whether your current episode of depression, including the feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest, has lasted for more than two years without any significant improvement lasting several months?

No, the intense depression and loss of interest haven't been going on for the full two years, but rather for about a year and a bit. While my overall struggles started almost two years ago, there was actually a brief stretch late last summer where my mood lifted slightly, even though the voices and paranoia persisted.

You mentioned the intense depression and loss of interest have been going on for about a year and a bit, can you tell me more about how this period of depression fits into the overall nearly two years since your troubles started?

The hopeless, drained feeling and loss of interest have actually been present for the vast majority of the nearly two years since my struggles first began. Aside from a few brief periods where I felt more numb than outright sad, this heavy depression has been a constant, dominating presence throughout most of this entire timeframe.

To clarify, has your current episode of depression, including the feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest, lasted for less than two years, and if so, did it start after a specific stressful event or change in your life?

Yes, the heavy depression and loss of interest have lasted for less than two years, specifically about a year and a bit. It started getting much worse after our clinic did a major electronic health record upgrade, which led to me taking on extra shifts just as my evening classes got a lot more difficult.
To confirm, your current episode of depression, with significant feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest, has been ongoing for approximately one year and a bit, correct?

Yes, that's correct, the heavy, hopeless feeling and losing interest in things like jogging and my Raspberry Pi projects have been going on for about a year and a bit. It really started to get bad after I took on those extra shifts at the clinic and my evening classes got a lot more demanding. I just feel completely drained trying to keep up with it all.
You've mentioned the depression has lasted for about a year and a bit, can you specify if there was a clear start to this episode or if it gradually developed over time?

It didn't start all at once, but rather developed gradually and got steadily worse over time. It really began building up after I started picking up those extra shifts at the clinic and my evening classes got more demanding. Eventually, that constant stress and exhaustion just turned into this heavy, hopeless feeling that hasn't gone away.

Have you had any previous episodes of depression before this current one that has lasted for about a year and a bit, or is this the first time you've experienced such persistent feelings of sadness and hopelessness?
No, I've never experienced anything like this before. This is the first time in my life that I've felt so completely hopeless and drained.
To confirm, you've had no periods of significant improvement lasting several months during this episode of depression that has lasted about a year and a bit, is that correct?

Yes, that is correct. I haven't had any long periods of feeling better; at most, there were just a few brief stretches where I felt more numb than deeply sad. The heavy, hopeless feeling has been pretty constant for this past year and a bit.
Can you describe any significant changes or variations in the intensity of your depressive symptoms over the past year and a bit, aside from the brief period where your mood lifted slightly?

Aside from those brief stretches where I felt more numb than outright sad, my low mood, loss of interest, and feelings of failure have just steadily gotten worse over the past year and a bit. It really ramped up and became much more intense after I started taking on extra shifts at the clinic and my evening classes got more difficult.

You mentioned this is your first episode of depression and it has lasted for about a year and a bit, can you tell me if you have experienced any psychotic symptoms such as hallucinations or delusions during this episode?

Yes, I've been convinced that the new charting system was designed to track my mistakes specifically so administration can pull my license, and I often hear a low male voice behind me telling me I'm screwing up when I'm alone or working late. These experiences have mostly happened at the exact same time as my heavy depression, and it feels like they've gone hand in hand for most of this past year and a half.
Can you describe in more detail the nature of the voice you hear and when exactly you hear it, such as during specific activities or times of the day?

It's a low male voice that sounds like it's right behind me, especially during late shifts at the clinic or when I'm home alone in a quiet room. He comments directly on what I'm doing, saying things like "You're screwing this up again" or "They know you're dangerous," even though there is never anyone there.
Have you ever experienced any periods where the voice stopped or significantly decreased in frequency, especially during the brief stretch last summer when your mood slightly improved?

No, the voice actually didn't stop or decrease during that time at all. Even though I didn't feel as depressed for those few weeks, I still kept hearing that male voice telling me I was dangerous and believed the charting system was tracking me.

Did the psychotic symptoms, such as hearing the voice, occur only during the periods when you were experiencing depressive symptoms, or did they also occur at times when your mood was slightly better?

Yes, they definitely occurred even when my mood was a bit better. During that stretch late last summer when I wasn't feeling quite as depressed, I still heard that male voice telling me I was dangerous and felt convinced the charting system was tracking my mistakes.
Did the psychotic symptoms, such as hearing the voice and believing in the tracking, precede the onset of your depressive symptoms or did they occur after the depression started?

They actually started and ramped up around the same time, so one didn't really come before the other. As the heavy depression and loss of interest set in, that was also when the voice and the feeling of being tracked really started to build. They have pretty much gone hand in hand from the very beginning.
Did the psychotic symptoms, such as hearing the voice and delusions, occur only during the depressive episodes or have they also occurred independently of your depressive mood?

Yes, they have occurred independently of my low mood too. During a stretch late last summer, my depression lifted a bit and I wasn't feeling quite as down, but I still heard that male voice calling me dangerous and believed the charting system was tracking me.
Have you experienced any periods where the depressive symptoms, such as feelings of sadness and hopelessness, were absent but the psychotic symptoms, like hearing the voice, were still present?

Yes, late last summer my mood lifted a bit and I wasn't feeling quite as depressed for a few weeks. But even though that heavy sadness was mostly gone during that time, I still heard that male voice calling me dangerous and remained convinced the charting system was tracking me.
Can you confirm if the voice you hear and the belief in being tracked have continued to the present day, or have they changed in intensity or frequency over time?

Yes, they have continued to the present day and remain a steady, ongoing problem. They started about a year and a half ago, a few months after the new charting system went live, and they haven't really let up. It's just been a constant part of what I've been struggling with for nearly two years now.
Have you ever had a period where the depressive symptoms, such as sadness and hopelessness, were completely gone, but the psychotic symptoms, like hearing the voice, persisted?

Yes, late last summer there was a stretch of a few weeks where the heavy sadness and hopelessness were mostly gone and my mood lifted. But even though the depression wasn't really there, I still heard that male voice calling me dangerous and remained convinced the charting system was tracking my mistakes.
Have you ever experienced a period where the voice stopped or you didn't believe in the tracking, but then came back, or have these psychotic symptoms been continuous since they started?

No, they have been pretty continuous and steady ever since they started about a year and a half ago. Even during that period late last summer when my mood lifted slightly and I felt less depressed, the voice and the belief about the tracking system remained just as active.
Did the psychotic symptoms, such as hearing the voice and believing in the tracking, ever occur in the absence of any depressive symptoms, or were they always accompanied by some level of depression?

Yes, they actually did occur without the depression. Late last summer, there was a stretch of a few weeks where my mood lifted and I didn't feel down or depressed at all, but I still heard that male voice and believed the charting system was tracking me. It was like those things were still completely active even when the sadness was gone.
Have you ever experienced any other types of psychotic symptoms besides hearing the voice and believing in the tracking, such as seeing things that aren't there or having unusual thoughts or beliefs?

No, I don't see things that aren't there; the voice is strictly auditory. However, my thoughts get extremely jumbled, to the point where I'll start answering a simple question in staff meetings and suddenly drift completely off-topic. I can hear myself losing track, but I just can't seem to pull my words back where they're supposed to be.

Can you describe if the voice you hear and your beliefs about being tracked are related to your depressive thoughts, or if they seem completely separate and unrelated to your feelings of sadness and hopelessness?

Most of the time they feel closely connected, because the voice criticizing me and the feeling of being tracked really feed into my feelings of worthlessness and failure. They ramped up together with the depression, but they also exist on their own, since I still experienced them last summer when my mood had lifted.
Do you think the voice you hear and your beliefs about being tracked are part of your depression, or do you think they are separate issues that you're dealing with?

Most of the time they feel connected because they started around the same time and really feed into my hopeless feelings. But since I still heard the voice and felt tracked late last summer when my depression lifted, it makes me think they might be somewhat separate issues.
Do you think the voice and your beliefs about being tracked would stop if your depression were successfully treated, or do you think they would continue even if your mood improved?

Honestly, I think they would continue even if my mood improved. Late last summer, my depression lifted a bit and I didn't feel as down, but I still heard that male voice and felt convinced the system was tracking me. It seems like those things don't just go away when the sadness does.
Do you think the voice and the feeling of being tracked are directly related to your depressive thoughts, or are they more about your perception of reality and the world around you?

I think it's a bit of both, because the paranoia and the heavy depression really ramped up together and have mostly gone hand-in-hand. But they also seem separate from my mood, since during that stretch last summer when I felt less depressed, I still heard the voice and felt convinced the system was tracking me. It is like that perception of what is happening around me stays there even when the sadness lifts.
Have you ever experienced any periods where the depressive symptoms completely resolved, but the psychotic symptoms, such as hearing the voice, persisted for more than two weeks?

Yes, that actually happened late last summer. There was a stretch of about three weeks where my mood lifted and I didn't feel depressed at all, but I still heard that critical male voice telling me I was dangerous and remained convinced the charting system was tracking me.
